newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian economy grew 3.25 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian economy grew 3.25 percent in 1996.

text.p: Nigeria's economy grew by 3.25 percent in 1996 based on preliminary GDP data, the federal office of statistics said on Wednesday.

It said in a report released through the official News Agency of Nigeria that the growth came from primary sectors of the economy such as agriculture, petroleum and gas and compares with GDP growth of 2.2 percent in 1995.
Nigeria is widely expected to record more significant growth if economic reforms in place since 1995 are maintained in this year's fiscal budget due to be announced in the next few days.
The reforms aim at gradually opening up the economy of Africa's most populous nation and have so far stabilised the exchange rate and reduced inflation to under 30 percent from 80 percent a year ago.
The 1997 budget is widely expected to announce the privatisation of some state firms in order to attract foreign investment and stimulate further economic growth.

The office of statistics said the contribution of imports to GDP last year fell substantially to 38.48 percent from 47.34 percent in 1995. "Consequently, net exports increased their share of GDP from -9.5 percent to -3.5 percent," it said.
